The petitioner is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 506 of IPC and Section 3 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The case of the prosecution is that the petitioners subjected defacto complainant to cruelty, both mentally and physically and also demanded the respondent No.2 to bring money from her parental home.
3. Both the parties are present before this Court.

entities.text: Mohammed Azharuddin Nadaf vs State By East Zone Women Police Station
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the criminal proceedings, petitioner No.1 and defacto complainant filed a joint memo, stating that they have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves.

In terms of the settlement, C.Mis.No.2/2020 has been withdrawn and they have agreed to dissolve their marriage mutually and respondent No.2 agreed to withdraw all the allegations against the petitioner and has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings.
5.

Though, the offences alleged are cognizable and uncompoundable in nature, however, having regard to the fact that both the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners are subjected to trial, since the probability of conviction is remote and bleak.
In view of the settlement, further continuation of criminal proceedings would an abuse of the process of law.

Accordingly I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
NC: 2023:KHC:45651 ii.
Impugned proceedings in CC No.14972/2023 on the file of VI Addl.
Chief Metropolitan
Magistrate Court Bangalore, stands quashed.

iii. Petitioner No.1, in terms of settlement has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.25 lakhs,
towards permanent alimony, out of which, Rs15 lakhs was already paid and today a demand draft of Rs.10 Lakhs is handed over to the defacto complainant before this Court, receipt of which is duly acknowledged,
subject to it's realization

. 
Sd/-
